# Vertical overlay: Chemical

**Level:** CISA critical infrastructure sector (child of NAICS 31-33 Manufacturing)
**Primary industry for Cris Santos Company:** NAICS 325998 All Other Miscellaneous Chemical Product and Preparation Manufacturing. Specialty chemical formulator and packager.
**Primary system:** Process control (DCS) and batch management system

## Regulators and sector risk management agency
SRMA: Department of Homeland Security (CISA); CISA Chemical Security (CFATS - authority lapsed; ChemLock voluntary program); U.S. Coast Guard (MTSA waterfront chemical facilities); EPA (Risk Management Program, 40 CFR Part 68 - process safety, not cyber-specific)

## Primary regulation for the gap analysis (P03)
**CFATS RBPS 8 (Cyber) - as voluntary benchmark**, 6 CFR 27.230(a)(8). Although unenforceable since the July 2023 lapse, RBPS 8 remains the only chemical-sector-specific federal cyber performance standard and is likely to return if CFATS is reauthorized. MTSA-regulated chemical terminals should instead gap against 33 CFR 101 Subpart F (binding).
Source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-6/section-27.230

## Sector context
- **Sensitive data:** Chemical-terrorism Vulnerability Information (CVI, 6 CFR 27.400) - legacy; SSI for MTSA facilities (49 CFR Part 1520); Process safety information and formulations; EAR-controlled chemical technology (e.g., CWC/Australia Group items); Employee PII
- **Critical systems:** DCS; Safety instrumented systems (SIS); PLCs/SCADA for tank farms and terminals; Laboratory information management systems; MES/ERP; Loading rack automation
- **Sector AI rules and guidance:** None identified beyond cross-sector obligations
- **Assurance alternatives to SOC 2:** None noted
- **Scenario incident (P08):** Intrusion into process control systems at a chemical facility
- **Scenario AI use case (P10):** Process-optimization model
